Re: Expert Witness Retention Agreement — Delgado v. Harrowgate Manufacturing Co., No. 2:25-cv-04412 (E.D. Pa.)

Dear Dr. Vosberg:

This letter confirms the terms on which Hollis & Parr LLP ("Counsel"), on behalf of its client Marisol Delgado ("Client"), retains Vosberg Forensic Engineering, LLC and you personally (together, "Expert") to provide expert consulting and, if designated, expert testimony in the above-captioned matter (the "Matter"). This Agreement takes effect on the date you countersign it.

1. Engagement. Expert is retained initially as a non-testifying consulting expert under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(4)(D). Counsel may later designate Expert as a testifying expert under Rule 26(a)(2). Expert shall not be designated as a testifying expert without Expert's agreement, and Expert shall notify Counsel promptly if Expert becomes unwilling to testify.

2. Scope of Work. Expert shall review the machine-guarding design, maintenance records, and incident materials produced in the Matter; inspect the subject press brake; perform such testing as Counsel approves in advance in writing; and form opinions on design defect, warnings, and causation. Expert shall not conduct destructive testing without Counsel's prior written approval and, where required, leave of court.

3. Fees and Expenses. Expert's rate is $475 per hour for review, analysis, and report preparation, and $650 per hour for deposition and trial testimony, including travel time at half rate. Expert shall submit itemized monthly invoices identifying the task, the date, and the time in tenths of an hour. Counsel shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt. Expert shall obtain Counsel's written approval before incurring any single expense over $2,500 or before exceeding a cumulative total of $60,000 in fees.

4. Retainer. Expert acknowledges receipt of a $15,000 retainer, to be held in Expert's business account and applied against the final invoices in the Matter. Any unearned balance shall be refunded within thirty (30) days after the conclusion of Expert's engagement.

5. Independence. Expert's compensation is not contingent on the outcome of the Matter, on the substance of Expert's opinions, or on the content of Expert's testimony. Expert's opinions shall be Expert's own, based on Expert's independent analysis of the materials and the applicable engineering standards.

6. Confidentiality and Work Product. All materials Counsel provides to Expert, and all drafts, notes, and communications Expert generates in the Matter, are confidential and, until Expert is designated as a testifying expert, are protected from disclosure under Rule 26(b)(4)(D) and the work-product doctrine. Expert shall not disclose them to anyone other than Expert's employees working on the Matter, each of whom Expert shall bind to these obligations. Expert shall comply with the Stipulated Protective Order entered in the Matter on March 4, 2026, and shall sign the acknowledgment it requires.

7. Draft Reports and Communications. Expert should be aware that, if designated, Rule 26(b)(4)(B) and (C) protect Expert's draft reports and most communications between Counsel and Expert, but do not protect the facts, data, or assumptions Counsel provided that Expert considered. Expert shall preserve all materials Expert considered in forming any opinion and shall produce them on Counsel's request.

8. Disclosure of Prior Testimony. Expert shall provide, and shall update on request, a current curriculum vitae, a list of all publications from the preceding ten (10) years, and a list of all cases in which Expert testified at trial or by deposition during the preceding four (4) years, as Rule 26(a)(2)(B) requires.

9. Conflicts. Expert represents that Expert has performed a conflicts check and has no engagement, financial interest, or relationship that conflicts with this retention, and shall notify Counsel immediately if one arises.

10. Client Is Not a Party to Fees. Counsel is responsible for Expert's fees under this Agreement. Expert shall look solely to Counsel, and not to Client, for payment.

11. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement on ten (10) days' written notice. Counsel shall pay for all work performed through the effective date of termination. Expert's obligations under Sections 6, 7 and 9 survive termination. On termination, Expert shall return or destroy all materials Counsel provided, at Counsel's election, except for one archival copy Expert may retain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Section 6.

12. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

13. Entire Agreement. This letter is the entire agreement between Counsel and Expert regarding the Matter and may be amended only in a writing signed by both.

If these terms are acceptable, please sign below and return one copy.

Sincerely,

HOLLIS & PARR LLP

By: /s/ Ruth Ellingham
Ruth Ellingham, Partner
